notes:
FN rows for hostap defects found by adjudication read-through, not by an aurora-lint finding. Per ADR-0007 as clarified 2026-09-23, a key and a label-basis reason are publishable regardless of the underlying defect's upstream status; each reason states only the construct and why it is a miss at that line.

SCOPE OF THIS BATCH. The first ten keys taken from hostap's public history: code the upstream project has since changed, each row citing the upstream commit that changed it. This batch was drawn before the scope correction above, so it covers only items with such a commit; it is not a statement about any other item.

KEY RULE. Each row is keyed at the access or dereference that the upstream fix protects, the line where the rule would report had it detected the defect, not at the guard the fix edits. This follows the rule already applied to EXP34-C (the dereference is the violation site). Where one fix covers two accesses (895fd588, two lines) or the same guard in two functions (7ce11243, drv_callbacks.c and ieee802_11.c), each access is its own row.

VERIFIED FOR EVERY ROW: (1) no existing row at the same (file, line, rule) on main at submission; (2) aurora-lint at aurora_lint_sha does not report the row's rule at that line over the pinned hostap commit (full-checkout scan, same invocation as the real-world runner). Some lines carry existing rows under OTHER rules (ARR37-C/ARR00-C/ARR36-C/INT14-C, all FP); those are untouched.

EXCLUDED, NOT FN. src/common/nan_de.c:651 (upstream ec339318, first batch): an INT33-C TP already sits at that key, so the rule did report it. The seven follow-up items the paper attributes to EXP34-C detections are tool findings, not misses.

HELD, NOT IN THIS BATCH (need a keying ruling). Three follow-up read-through fixes whose dereference is not in the function the fix edits: wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface.c (upstream f3b1fc3b: the NULL reaches a libc string call, so the dereference is outside the corpus), src/eap_server/eap_server_peap.c (upstream 0da59aad: the dereference is inside a shared inline accessor in a header), wpa_supplicant/wnm_sta.c (upstream e341c11d: the dereference is inside a callee in events.c). Each sits next to an 'FP as keyed' caller-argument row, and that standard says a positional argument is not a violation site, so where their FN key belongs is a ruling, not a mechanical choice.

NOT IN THIS BATCH. The remaining hostap audit-logged defects: they follow in later batches under the same key rule, once their construct-level detail is in hand on this node.

No recall figure follows from this batch until it merges and the sync runs.
